title: Korean-Style Beef Rice Bowls
subtitle: sweet-savoury ground beef with garlic, ginger and sesame over jasmine rice with crisp cucumber and carrot, all mild
imageAlt: Glossy browned ground beef over rice with sliced cucumber and shredded carrot and sesame seeds in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Start the rice first; the beef takes 12 minutes.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Vegetables
steps.text: While the rice cooks, thinly slice the cucumber and shred the carrots.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar and sesame oil together.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Cook the beef in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, 7–8 minutes, until browned with no pink and 71°C (160°F). Spoon off the fat.

steps.title: Garlic and ginger
steps.text: Push the beef aside, add the garlic and ginger to the pan and cook 1 minute until fragrant, then stir through.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Pour in the sauce and simmer 2–3 minutes, stirring, until it's absorbed and the beef looks glossy.

steps.title: Bowls
steps.text: Rice in each bowl, then the beef, cucumber and carrot, with sesame seeds on top.

fixIt.fix: Use low-sodium soy sauce, and add a squeeze of lime or a little more sugar to balance.
Let the pan get hot first and leave the beef alone for 2 minutes before breaking it up.
Add it only after the beef has browned, and keep it moving for just 1 minute.

saleTip: Lean ground beef in 1 kg family packs is the best value at No Frills; freeze it in 680 g flat bags.
swap: Lean ground turkey or pork: same method, cooked to 74°C (165°F) for turkey or 71°C (160°F) for pork.
leftovers: Pack beef and rice together, vegetables separate; add them cold after reheating.
doneness: Ground beef at 71°C (160°F) with no pink (Health Canada, ground beef).
source: Based on tested Korean-style ground beef bowl methods (Budget Bytes, Allrecipes): browned ground beef glazed with soy, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic and ginger. Gochujang left out to keep it mild.
prepAhead: Mix the sauce and cut the vegetables up to 1 day ahead.
The cooked beef freezes for quick lunches.
reheat: Beef and rice covered in the microwave with a splash of water, 2 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Garlic-soy beef over rice with carrots; no ginger, cucumber or sesame seeds.

fancy.note: Quick-pickled cucumber and a fried egg on each bowl.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: toss the sliced cucumber with the rice vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt; let it sit while you cook.

addSteps.title: Fried eggs
addSteps.text: Fry the eggs in the oil over medium, covered, 3–4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are firm, and set one on each bowl.

plating: Rice in the bowl, beef on one side.
Cucumber and carrot in their own piles.
Egg in the middle, sesame seeds over everything.

why.1-1: Brown sugar gives the caramel sweetness of bulgogi without hours of marinating.
why.1-2: Toasted sesame oil is the flavour that makes it taste Korean; a little goes a long way.
why.2-2: Cool, crisp cucumber balances the rich, sweet beef.

funFact: 'Bulgogi' means 'fire meat' in Korean; this weeknight version borrows its sweet soy-sesame flavour without the grill.
